description:
INTERNAL ALTERATIONS TO CONVERT EXISTING 5-BEDROOM
HOUSE (C3) INTO 9-ROOM H.M.O.(C4) 
WITH ASSOCIATED AMENITIES
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed development, by reason of the excessive number of occupiers that it accommodates, represents an overly intensive use of the site which would be likely to give rise to undue levels of disturbance and noise to adjoining occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies D3.D(5), (7), (9), and (10), D13 and D14 of The London Plan (2021) and GR1C, HO10(4) and strategic policy 01 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</p>

<p>The proposed conversion of the property into a 9-bedroom Large House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) would be unacceptable in principle due to the site’s poor accessibility to public transport and essential services, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024) and policy HO10(2) and (3) and strategic policy 03(7) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance (2023) and the Residential Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of its poor internal layout which would have adverse vertical stacking issues and has not demonstrated if sufficient shared amenity spaces have been provided, would result in poor standard of accommodation, detrimental to future occupiers by way of limited outlook, privacy and light to bedrooms and communal areas. This is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies D3 and D6 The London Plan (2021), GR1C and HO10(5), (6), (7) and (9) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance (2023).</p>

<p>No evidence has been provided to demonstrate the that the proposed change of use of the site would be car-free and that the increase in the number of occupants would not result in any adverse impacts on traffic and parking congestion on street. Although the future occupants could be inclined to use public transport, as no parking permit free legal agreement has been agreed and signed between the applicant and the Council, the proposal would not restrict car parking provision in line with existing levels of public transport accessibility and connectivity contrary to the policies T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan and M2 and Strategic Policy 10 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</p>
